findings.evidence: Compare crates/oqueue-broker/src/join_group/round/close.rs's record of two liveness re-checks deleted because each could be deleted with the suite still green, against close_on_deadline's publish, which has exactly that property and is kept. Neither sentence names the distinction that reconciles them: the deleted branches were redundant in every execution, this one only in single-threaded ones. Separately, backlog.md's justifying clause -- 'only reachable under an interleaving a deterministic test cannot construct' -- is falsifiable: plan::plan_join is pub(super) in round and GroupJoins::lock is private to round, so round::tests can enrol under the lock, drop it without publishing, then call close_on_deadline; the assertion would be on SyncGroups::rebalance_timeout, which sync_group/tests/deadline.rs already asserts on throughout. NOT EXECUTED -- a reading of visibility, not a measurement. Graded minor against the reviewer's stated instinct: the shipped code is correct on every path traced, nothing client-observable changes by acting, and cargo-mutants emits no mutant for a deleted call statement, so no gate can fail here.

findings.evidence: Rule 9: 'document the fixed order beside the types, not in a comment nobody will find when adding the third lock.' The order GroupJoins::entries -> SyncGroups::entries -> Assignments is stated in join_group/round/mod.rs and twice in sync_wait.rs and nowhere else. The three type docs carry none of it: GroupJoins says 'Every group's own join-round state'; SyncGroups says 'Every group's own assignment barrier'; Assignments has twenty lines about visibility and nothing about ordering. Rule 9 has no gate. M4.87 is the commit that found the order was a chain rather than a pair and left the finding in the comments the rule tells you not to rely on.

findings.evidence: backlog.md: "Not 'publish inside plan_and_join's final lock scope' ... the Step::Close arm returns out of the loop without re-entering it -- so the round-closing member ... would publish nothing." plan_join assigns round.members = trial before it decides Step::Close, and that assignment runs inside the scoped lock block in round/mod.rs. A publish at the end of that block therefore runs on the pass that returns Step::Close, with the round-closing member already in the roster, and would publish 300 s rather than nothing. notes: The terminating round, second attempt: the first was regraded after the per-commit review of its own artifact found it had graded a client-observable race minor. This one verified the repair rather than the prose. The race is closed on every path a round can close on: finalize_close has exactly two call sites and both publish under the guard that took the roster; close_generation is the only caller of JoinBarrierComplete and its Illegal/Unavailable arms advance no generation and correctly publish nothing. Neither new site can write a wrong value -- finalize_close's early already.clone() branch is unreachable while a slot is held, entry.open cannot be replaced across close_generation's await -- not because install_round has one caller, which the per-commit review of this artifact disproved (apply_open calls it too), but because the slot does it: open_holding_slot owns a SlotGuard across apply_open and both close paths hold the slot. ⚠️ And NOT because neither write can lower the standing value, which the same review disproved: a group whose previous roster is {D}, with D rejoining at 6 s after a round that closed at 300 s, empties awaiting and returns Step::Close without reaching join's trailing publish, so apply_close writes fold({D(6s)}) = 6 s over a standing 300 s. M4.83's 'a parked follower is never shortened' property still holds, but it rests on sync_group.rs reading the value once at park time rather than on any monotonicity of the writes. close_on_deadline's publish is genuinely unreachable in any single-threaded sequence -- after plan_join enrols there is no await before publish_sync_wait, so the enrolled-but-unpublished window opens only when another thread takes the rounds mutex in the gap -- but finding 1 records that the row's claim about testability is stronger than the visibility rules support. The handoff undo is complete: roadmap.md and M5.md both read eight ids and record the ninth's removal, `grep -rn M4.87 docs/ scripts/ .agents/` finds no document still describing it as handed on, check-milestone-handoff.sh --milestone M4 exits 0, and the backlog's bucket counts still add up with M4.87 moved into the repairs bucket. m4-complete.sh: this tree can satisfy it -- leg 0 fails today only because this commit is unread, which this artifact clears, and the artifact commit touches only reviews/ so milestone_commits excludes it; leg 0b is green; cargo test -p oqueue-broker is 321 passed, 0 failed.
